Definition: of foreign origin (H7248); a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician:--sorcerer, wise man.
BiblicalUsage: Magos is the Magian, the wise man of the east, and the same word names both the worshippers and the sorcerer. Matthew 2:1 has wise men coming from the east to Jerusalem, and Matthew 2:7 and Matthew 2:16 have Herod calling them privily and then raging when they mock him. Acts 13:6 turns the word dark: Elymas the sorcerer withstands Paul, seeking to turn the deputy from the faith.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two uses of this word are the test of all wisdom: the wise men of Matthew 2:1 followed the star to Christ, while Elymas in Acts 13:6 used his knowledge to turn men away from Him. My position is that true wisdom always ends in worship, and false wisdom always ends in opposition.
